name: American Circuits
old_description: American Circuits is an electronic contract manufacturer headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, providing turnkey printed circuit board assembly across two Charlotte facilities.
about:
American Circuits operates from Charlotte, North Carolina, where it has maintained a family-run, minority-owned electronic contract manufacturing business for more than three decades. The company was founded by Vic Gondha, a first-generation immigrant who built the firm after arriving in the United States with a goal of owning a business that could support his family and community. His son, Ket Gondha, now serves as CEO, having expanded the company's Charlotte campus after a career on Wall Street.

The firm provides turnkey printed circuit board assembly from two facilities encompassing roughly 40,000 square feet. Its capabilities span PCB fabrication and assembly (surface-mount, through-hole, and mixed technology), rapid prototyping, conformal coating and potting, automated optical inspection, PCB design and reverse engineering, design-for-manufacturability analysis, bill-of-materials optimization, custom wire harness and cable assembly, and full electro-mechanical integration including box builds and subassemblies. Production runs range from single prototypes to volumes exceeding 100,000 units.

American Circuits serves approximately 400 customers across defense, healthcare, robotics, LED lighting, security and key-control systems, and automotive sectors. Named clients include TE Connectivity, Honda, and Assa Abloy. The company emphasizes a one-stop model that controls the process from bare-board procurement through final assembly and test.

The founder's vision centered on offering both bare boards and turnkey assemblies under one roof—a combination he described as rare in the U.S. market. That end-to-end control, coupled with flexible low-to-high volume runs and ITAR-registered, ISO 9001-certified operations, remains the core differentiator the company highlights today.
